Apple joins the race for AI agents that control your device while raising new barriers for competitors
After Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google launched their own AI agents, Apple is now building one too - while making it harder for rivals to access its devices. According to a job listing, Apple is hiring a senior engineer to lead the project as a rival to Muse, Dots, Duet, and Grok Bots. Privacy is expected to be central to the new agent, with permission models and sandboxing (protected test environments).
According to Bloomberg, the agent could arrive as early as late next year, though it remains in an early stage. Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, is pushing software chief Craig Federighi toward a bolder AI strategy, the report says. After many delays, the company recently rolled out generative AI features for Siri. The road to that release was marked by internal rifts and staff departures.
Meanwhile, macOS 27.3 now requires 14 steps instead of four for users to let third-party agents like ChatGPT control their Macs. Apple says the change protects users, though some AI companies and users see it as an effort to slow down competitors, Bloomberg reports.
